summary: Cuba's foreign ministry issues tourists a tourist card (tourist visa) for a single entry and a 90-day stay, extendable once for the same period, which can be applied for online; it publishes no list of the nationalities that need it. Every traveler arriving through an airport must also complete the D'Viajeros arrival form, and Canada's travel advice says you must show proof of medical insurance on entry.

declarations.name: D'Viajeros traveler information form
declarations.submitWindow: From 72 hours before arrival until immigration; passengers are asked to complete it 48 hours in advance
declarations.text: Every traveller entering Cuba through an airport, Cuban or foreign, must fill in the D'Viajeros form, which replaces the paper arrival card, customs declaration and health affidavit. Each family member, children included, needs their own form, and a new one is needed for every trip. It can be filled in from 72 hours before arrival until you reach immigration, and passengers are told to complete it 48 hours in advance: airlines check that it has been done before boarding. The QR code it generates is shown to the health and customs authorities on arrival, printed or on a phone.

source.name: Cuba Ministry of Transport — D'Viajeros advance traveller information form, Personal Data step (questions and answers shown with the form)

currencyLimits.text: Declare foreign currency worth more than USD 5,000 when you bring it into Cuba. The Cuban peso cannot be exchanged outside Cuba, and exchanging money anywhere other than a Cadeca exchange house is illegal.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Cuba travel advice (entry requirements)

notes: Drones are not allowed into Cuba. The UK FCDO and the Government of Canada say they are confiscated on arrival; the FCDO says they are not returned until your departure.

The UK FCDO says GPS devices are subject to import requirements (turn off the GPS on phones, tablets and laptops), photography equipment may need an import licence, and some electrical items with heavy power consumption may be confiscated on entry.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says Cuba's Central Bank has announced that international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are no longer accepted, that you cannot withdraw cash from ATMs with an international card, and that the available payment methods are cash and Cuban prepaid cards. It advises bringing enough cash, US dollars or euros, for the whole stay and for emergencies, and says exchanging money anywhere other than a Cadeca exchange house is illegal.

source.name: UK FCDO — Cuba travel advice (safety and security: money)

safety.text: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to Cuba. Repeated collapses of the national electricity grid and shortages of fuel, electricity, water and basic necessities disrupt transport, medical care and communications, and have led to frequent protests. Cuba's international airports have run out of aviation fuel, only Terminal 3 at Havana's José Martí airport is operating, and several airlines have suspended flights. Opportunistic crime is rising, including muggings in Havana, though overall levels remain lower than in the UK.

tips.text: Bring all the money you will need in cash. The UK FCDO says Cuba's Central Bank has announced that international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are no longer accepted, and that you cannot withdraw cash from ATMs with an international card. US dollars and euros are widely accepted and can be exchanged in Cuba.

Australia's travel advice says that if you have travelled to Cuba since January 2021, you are not eligible for the US Visa Waiver Program, and the UK FCDO says you cannot travel from Cuba to the USA without a US visa.

US regulations (31 CFR 515.560) authorize travel-related transactions with Cuba only for 12 categories of activity, including support for the Cuban people, and nothing in them authorizes tourist travel. Records of the travel transactions must be kept for at least 10 years (31 CFR 501.601).

Fill in the D'Viajeros form in the 72 hours before you arrive. The UK FCDO says to show the QR code on arrival in electronic or printed form, and to download or print the completed form, as wifi may not be available on arrival.
Canada's travel advice says you must show proof of medical insurance on entry, and that if you cannot show acceptable proof, you may have to buy cover from a Cuban insurer on arrival.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cuba?
faq.answer: Cuba's foreign ministry issues tourists a tourist card (tarjeta del turista), which it calls a tourist visa: valid for a single entry and a 90-day stay, extendable once for the same period, and available online through the eVisa-Cuba site or at a Cuban consulate. It publishes no list of the nationalities that need it or are exempt, so this site shows the rule only for passports whose own government's travel advice states it.

faq.question: Can US citizens travel to Cuba?
faq.answer: Not as tourists. US regulations (31 CFR 515.560) authorize travel-related transactions with Cuba only for 12 categories of activity, including support for the Cuban people, and nothing in them authorizes tourist travel; records must be kept for at least 10 years (31 CFR 501.601). The UK FCDO says international cards such as Visa and Mastercard are no longer accepted in Cuba.

faq.question: Does visiting Cuba affect US ESTA?
faq.answer: Australia's travel advice says that if you have travelled to Cuba since January 2021, you are not eligible for the US Visa Waiver Program, and the UK FCDO says you cannot travel from Cuba to the USA without a US visa.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Cuba?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says you must show proof of medical insurance to enter Cuba, and that if you cannot, or your proof is not accepted, you may have to buy cover from a Cuban insurer on arrival. No Cuban government page we could read states the rule.

faq.question: What is the D'Viajeros form?
faq.answer: It is Cuba's online arrival form. The UK FCDO says you must complete it on the D'Viajeros portal within 72 hours before entering Cuba and show the QR code it emails you on arrival; airlines check it at check-in. Holders of an electronic visa enter its code on the form.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Cuba?
faq.answer: Yes. Cuba's foreign ministry says the tourist card can be extended once for the same period of 90 days, and that for the procedure you should ask at your hotel's desk or go directly to the immigration authorities. The UK FCDO says you could be detained if you overstay.
